note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a SLK 7(1); A06b SLK 7(1); L05 SLK 9(1)(b)): ordinary naturalisation after 8 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Slovakia, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Slovakia for 8 consecutive years immediately prior to the application or 10 years with a permanent residence permit. ... n.a. ... Note: Person who acquires citizenship of another country otherwise than by birth or marriage loses Slovak citizenship except if that person has legally resided in that other country for at least five years at the time of acquiring the foreign citizenship. Due to this broad exception ground, citizenship is in principle not lost upon acquisition of a foreign citizenship in practice.
